text:
arjun: heads up — macos-integration CI is red after the recent lockfile regen merged in #4123. Failing set: ~20 tests, mostly timeouts in the httpx pool tests and a few async loop teardown errors. looks transitive, not our code. anyone picked this up yet?

ci-bot: Build failed: https://ci.redwood.internal/2387654321/jobs/142 (macos-integration)

kevin: saw the failure. quick glance shows a different httpcore wheel was pulled in. could be a transitive resolution change from the lock regen.

laura: I can try a quick local repro on my macbook. which commit should I start from?

arjun: start from the merge commit (sha: b3f7d2c). ideally we want to bisect which top-level bump led to the transitive change.

kevin: plan: revert to the previous lockfile locally, then `poetry lock` against each bumped top-level dep to see which one produces the new httpcore/httpx. that narrows it down faster than a full git bisect.

laura: ack. trying now. sharing commands I'm running so others can reproduce: 
```bash
git checkout b3f7d2c~1 
cp poetry.lock /tmp/old.lock
# regenerate lock with the new top-level bump applied one-by-one
poetry add httpx@0.24.0 --no-update || true
poetry lock --no-update
python -m pip install -e .[tests]
pytest tests/integration/test_http_pool.py::test_timeout -q
```

arjun: thanks laura. if you can't repro locally it's probably CI-only (mac runner quirk). either way, if the lock regen caused a newer httpcore wheel with a different backlog behavior, that would explain the timeouts.

laura: partial repro — I can trigger the timeout locally after forcing httpcore 0.17.0 -> 0.18.0. interestingly, the wheel on macos has a different C extension build flags, so behavior diverges.

kevin: great find. can you capture the `pip freeze` and the wheel tags? e.g. `python -c "import httpcore; import importlib.metadata as m; print(m.version('httpcore'))"` and `pip debug --verbose` to see tags.

laura: done — httpcore==0.18.0, wheel tags show macosx_11_0_x86_64. attaching snippet: `httpcore 0.18.0 macosx_11_0_x86_64`

arjun: sounds like the lock regen pulled in a build-specific wheel that we didn't see before. options: 1) pin httpcore to 0.17.x in our lockfile until upstream fixes, 2) add a CI step to prefer universal/wheelless build, or 3) revert the lockfile bump and do a more careful staged bump.

kevin: I'd prefer a quick mitigation: pin httpcore <=0.17.* in the lockfile and cut a lock regen PR that forces that constraint. then run CI matrix to confirm. if that passes we can do a staged bump in a separate PR where we coordinate macos build.

laura: I can open the PR after I run the full integration suite locally. ETA ~30min.

arjun: thanks. @kevin can you run the macos CI rerun once laura posts the PR? also, let's add a short note in the PR describing the transitive wheel discrepancy so infra knows.

kevin: will do. also leaving a bisect note — if pinning doesn't work we should try this script to automate lockfile bisect: 
```bash
# checkout base commit (pre-regen)
# for each top-level dep in bumps.txt do
#   apply bump (poetry add <pkg>@<ver> --no-update)
#   poetry lock --no-update
#   run the failing pytest
#   record whether failure reproduced
```

arjun: perfect. Laura or Kevin please paste the minimal failing pytest invocation in the PR so QA can run it locally. i'll mark this high priority. :pray:

laura: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4187 — includes pin + description + reproducer cmd. kicks off CI now.

ci-bot: Rerun started for PR #4187 (macos-integration).

kevin: monitoring. if CI still flakes i'll start the lockfile bisect script and loop folks in. thanks all. :thumbsup:
